topic: How does the 45° scan range affect link budget calculations for edge-of-coverage users compared to broadside beams?
consensus_response: The 45° scan range significantly impacts link budget calculations for edge-of-coverage users due to increased path loss, reduced received signal power, and higher sidelobe levels (SLLs). Compared to broadside beams, the 45° scan range reduces beamwidth, increases SLLs, and introduces more interference. Frequency-selective adaptive beamforming can mitigate these effects by optimizing the antenna pattern for specific frequency bands, thereby minimizing SLLs and improving link budget calculations. Doppler shift compensation integrated with FSAB further improves link budget calculations and QoS for edge-of-coverage users.
